FN-DWSQHN-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 175
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Danny Garrett
Analyst: JT Mathis Date: 05/23/2023
House Bill 175 as introduced would increase the obligations of the Education Trust Fund by an
estimated $1 billion for fiscal year 2023 by providing a one-time tax rebate check to certain
qualified individual income taxpayers in an amount equal to: (1) $400 for taxpayers that are
married filing separate, head of family, or single; or (2) $800 for taxpayers that are married
filing jointly. This bill would provide that this rebate shall not constitute taxable income for
Alabama income tax purposes.
Further, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of the Department by an
estimated $1.1 million to mail these rebate checks to approximately 1.9 million taxpayers within
90 days of the effective date of this bill.

FN-DWSQHN-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 175
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Danny Garrett
Analyst: JT Mathis Date: 05/24/2023
House Bill 175 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education would increase the
obligations of the Education Trust Fund by an estimated $546 million for fiscal year 2023 by
providing a one-time refundable income tax credit check to certain qualified individual income
taxpayers to partially offset the amount of sales tax paid on groceries in an amount equal to: (1)
$210 for taxpayers that are married filing separate, head of family, or single; or (2) $420 for
taxpayers that are married filing jointly. This bill would provide that this tax credit shall not
constitute taxable income for Alabama income tax purposes.
Further, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of the Department by an
estimated $1.1 million to mail these tax credit checks to approximately 1.9 million taxpayers
within 90 days of the effective date of this bill.

FN-DWSQHN-3
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 175
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Representative Danny Garrett
Analyst: JT Mathis Date: 05/31/2023
House Bill 175 as passed the House of Representatives would increase the obligations of the
Education Trust Fund by an estimated $546 million for fiscal year 2023 by providing a one-time
refundable income tax credit check to certain qualified individual income taxpayers to partially
offset the amount of sales tax paid on groceries in an amount equal to: (1) $210 for taxpayers
that are married filing separate, head of family, or single; or (2) $420 for taxpayers that are
married filing jointly. This bill provides that this tax credit shall not constitute taxable income
for Alabama income tax purposes.
Further, this bill requires the Department of Revenue to electronically deposit the income tax
credit into the bank account of the qualified taxpayers based on the information indicated from
their return submitted for the taxable year that began January 1, 2021, and would increase the
administrative obligations of the Department by an estimated $230,000 to mail tax credit checks
to taxpayers that the Department does not have bank account information for, no sooner than
November 30, 2023.

FN-DWSQHN-4
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 175
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Representative Danny Garrett
Analyst: JT Mathis Date: 05/31/2023
House Bill 175 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education would
increase the obligations of the Education Trust Fund by an estimated $390 million for fiscal year
2023 by providing a one-time refundable income tax credit check to certain qualified individual
income taxpayers to partially offset the amount of sales tax paid on groceries in an amount equal
to: (1) $150 for taxpayers that are married filing separate, head of family, or single; or (2) $300
for taxpayers that are married filing jointly. This bill provides that this tax credit shall not
constitute taxable income for Alabama income tax purposes.
Further, this bill requires the Department of Revenue to electronically deposit the income tax
credit into the bank account of the qualified taxpayers based on the information indicated from
their return submitted for the taxable year that began January 1, 2021; and to mail tax credit
checks to taxpayers that the Department does not have bank account information for, no sooner
than November 30, 2023. These requirements would increase the obligations of the Department
by an undetermined amount; however, any increased obligation could be offset, in part or in
whole, by any interest that may accrue to the Refundable Tax Credit Fund, pursuant to the
provisions of this bill.
